{{nihongo|'''Kawara Shrine'''|香春神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Buzen Province]].

'''Kawara Shrine'''（かわらじんじゃ）is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Kawara, Fukuoka|arz|كاوارا|ceb|Kawara Machi|de|Kawara (Fukuoka)|fa|کاوارا، فوکوئوکا|fr|Kawara (Fukuoka)|it|Kawara|ja|香春町|ko|가와라정|ms|Kawara, Fukuoka|my|ခဝရမြို့၊ ဖူကူအိုကာ|pl|Kawara|ru|Кавара|tl|Kawara, Fukuoka|tr|Kawara|ur|کاوارا، فوکوکا|zh|香春町|qid=Q573632}}, {{ill|Tagawa District, Fukuoka|de|Tagawa-gun (Fukuoka)|fr|District de Tagawa|id|Distrik Tagawa, Fukuoka|it|Distretto di Tagawa|ja|田川郡|ko|다가와군|ms|Daerah Tagawa, Fukuoka|pl|Powiat Tagawa|zh|田川郡|qid=Q1156353}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|Q123258|qid=Q123258}}. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinai small shrine}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|ja|社格|ko|사격 (신토)|zh|社格|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha}}.

=== Overview ===
There are six shrines of Buzen Province listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}; three of them are at Kawara Shrine{{Efn2|The remaining three are all within {{ill|Usa Jingū|Q715632|qid=Q715632}}.}}. The three are Karakuni-Okinaga-Ōhime-Ōme Shrine, Oshihone Shrine, and Toyobika Shrine, which originally stood on the summits of the three Kawara mountains (Ichinodake, Ninodake, and Sannodake){{Efn2|It is said that Karakuni-Okinaga-Ōhime-Ōme Shrine was on Ichinodake, Oshihone Shrine on Ninodake, and Toyobika Shrine on Sannodake, though there are alternate theories.}}.

In {{ill|Wadō (era)|ar|وادو (حقبة)|de|Wadō (Ära)|es|Wadō|fa|وادو (دوره)|fr|Ère Wadō|ia|Wado|id|Wadō|ja|和銅|ko|와도|pt|Wadō (era)|ru|Вадо|simple|Wadō (era)|sr|Вадо (ера)|th|วาโด|tr|Wadō|uk|Вадо (ненґо)|zh|和銅|zh_yue|和銅|qid=Q1373026}} 2 ({{ill|709|Q23514|qid=Q23514}}), the three summit shrines were moved to the current site, creating present-day Kawara Shrine. Since ancient times it stood, with {{ill|Usa Jingū|Q715632|qid=Q715632}}, as one of Buzen's major shrines.
Karakuni-Okinaga-Ōhime-Ōme Shrine and Oshihone Shrine received {{ill|Senior First Rank|fa|شوئیچی|ja|正一位|ko|정1위|zh|正一位|qid=Q11123258}} in {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|de|Jōwa|es|Jōwa (período Heian)|fa|جووا (دوره هی‌آن)|fr|Ère Jōwa (Heian)|ia|Jowa|id|Jōwa|ja|承和 (日本)|ko|조와 (834년)|ru|Дзёва (Хэйан)|simple|Jōwa (Heian period)|sr|Џова (Хејан период)|tr|Jōwa (Heian)|uk|Дзьова (ненґо)|zh|承和 (日本)|zh_yue|承和|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} 10 ({{ill|843|Q23469|qid=Q23469}}), notably earlier than the dates when Nara's {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|Q705542|qid=Q705542}} (859), {{ill|Isonokami Jingū|Q708859|qid=Q708859}} (868), and {{ill|Ōyamato Shrine|abstract|Q245731|fr|Ōyamato-jinja|ja|大和神社|ru|Ооямато-дзиндзя|simple|Ōyamato Shrine|zh|大和神社|qid=Q245731}} (897) reached Senior First Rank.

Kawara Shrine had very high status in the early {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}. While Buzen's ichinomiya is generally considered Usa Jingū, some old materials record Kawara Shrine as ichinomiya<ref>Yuzuru Miura, ''National Shrine Directory'', National Shrine Directory Publication Society</ref>.

The priesthood has been successively held by the Akazome and Tsuruga families.

=== Enshrined deities ===
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Karakuni-Okinaga-Ōhime-Ōjime-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Oshihone-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Toyobime-no-Mikoto}} 

The {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Sandai Džicuroku|de|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fa|نیهون ساندای جیتسوروکو|ff|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon sandai jitsuroku|it|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|ko|일본삼대실록|pt|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ru|Нихон сандай дзицуроку|simple|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|zh|日本三代實錄|zh_classical|日本三代實錄|qid=Q1052981}} identifies Toyobime-no-Mikoto with Karakuni-Okinaga-Ōhime-Ōme-no-Mikoto.

An inscription before the shrine states: "First seat: Karakuni-Okinaga-Ōhime-Ōjime-no-Mikoto, who in the age of the gods crossed to Tang lands and returned in the reign of Emperor Sujin to be enshrined at the First Peak of Takawa District, Buzen. Second seat: Oshihone-no-Mikoto, child of Amatsuhi-Ōmikami, whose rough spirit manifested at the Second Peak. Third seat: Toyobime-no-Mikoto, maternal grandmother of Emperor Jinmu and mother of Sumiyoshi Ōmyōjin, enshrined at the Third Peak."

In extant fragments of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Buzen Fudoki}}, Karakuni-Okinaga-Ōhime-Ōjime-no-Mikoto is described as a deity who came from Silla<ref>{{Cite book|和書|title=History of Japanese Buddhism|date=1944-11-30|publisher=Iwanami Shoten|page=261|author=Zennosuke Tsuji}}</ref>.

The relation between Karakuni-Okinaga-Ōhime-Ōjime-no-Mikoto and {{ill|Empress Jingū|ar|الإمبراطورة جينغو|arz|الامبراطوره جينجو|az|Cinqu|bcl|Empress Jingū|ca|Jingu|cs|Džingú|de|Jingū|es|Jingū|eu|Jingū enperatriza|fa|امپراتریس جینگو|fr|Jingū|hr|Jingū (japanska carica)|hu|Dzsingú japán császárnő|id|Permaisuri Jingū|it|Jingū|ja|神功皇后|ka|ძინგუ|ko|진구 황후|nl|Jingu|pl|Jingū|pt|Jingu|ru|Императрица Дзингу|sh|Carica Jingū|si|ජින්ගූ අධිරාජිනිය|simple|Empress Jingū|sl|Cesarica Džingu|sv|Jingu Kogo|te|రాణి జింగూ|th|จักรพรรดินีจิงงู|tl|Emperatris Jingū|tr|Jingū (imparatoriçe)|uk|Імператриця Дзінґу|uz|Imperator Jingū|vi|Thiên hoàng Jingū|zh|神功皇后|zh_min_nan|Sîn-kong Hông-hō͘|zh_yue|神功皇后|qid=Q232803}} has long been discussed. Empress Jingū, mother of {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ar|الإمبراطور أوجين|arz|الامبراطور اوجين|azb|اوجین (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট ওজিন|cs|Ódžin|de|Ōjin|es|Ōjin Tennō|eu|Ōjin enperadorea|fa|امپراتور اوجین|fi|Ōjin|fr|Ōjin|hr|Ōjin|id|Kaisar Ōjin|it|Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|ka|ოძინი|ko|오진 천황|nl|Ojin|pl|Ōjin|pt|Ojin|ru|Император Одзин|sh|Car Ōjin|simple|Emperor Ōjin|sl|Cesar Odžin|sv|Ojin|th|จักรพรรดิโอจิง|tl|Emperador Ōjin|tr|Ōjin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Одзін|uz|Imperator Ōjin|vi|Thiên hoàng Ōjin|yo|Emperor Ōjin|zh|应神天皇|zh_min_nan|Ôzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|應神天皇|qid=Q317997}}, appears in the {{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}} as Okinagatarashihime-no-Mikoto / Ōtarashihime-no-Mikoto. "Karakuni" also resonates with Korea where she is linked in tradition to the {{ill|Three Han Campaign|Q11249435|qid=Q11249435}}. Some works identify the two as the same deity<ref>Tsuneari Ito, ''Dazaikanai-shi'', Rekishi Tosho Sha</ref>.

=== Divine ranks ===
Karakuni-Okinaga-Ōhime-Ōjime Shrine - Senior First Rank（Jōwa 10）
Oshihone Shrine - Senior First Rank（Jōwa 10）
Toyobika Shrine - Senior Second Rank（{{ill|Kennin|Q1195433|qid=Q1195433}} 1）

=== Crest ===
Triple-step lozenge; there is a theory this was granted by the {{ill|Kokura Domain|Q1140943|qid=Q1140943}} lord {{ill|Ogasawara clan|de|Ogasawara (Klan)|fa|خاندان اوگاساوارا|fr|Clan Ogasawara|it|Clan Ogasawara|ja|小笠原氏|ko|오가사와라씨|pt|Clã Ogasawara|ru|Огасавара (род)|qid=Q2975340}}.
